# Export the whole library and delete the account

## Intent

The owner's library belongs to the owner. This package lets the owner, and only the owner, take all of it out at any time as one JSON document — every link in every state with everything the library knows about it, every workspace, topic and tag, and a way to fetch each stored snapshot and reader view — and leave for good: deleting the account removes every piece of the owner's data, from database rows to stored snapshots and the AI key, within minutes and without undo, while nothing still running in the background can bring any of it back.

## Goals

- The whole library can be exported as a single JSON file, and the account with all its data deleted, by the owner alone.
- The export holds every link (all fields, all states, manual edits, use counts), workspace, topic and tag of the user; snapshots are not included in the JSON but each link carries a URL from which its snapshot and reader view can be fetched with the same token.
- For 20,000 links the export completes in under 60 seconds.
- Account deletion removes every link, snapshot, workspace, token, session and the stored AI provider key of the user, and the user record with them, within 10 minutes; the user is signed out immediately; there is no undo.
- No request, background job or search can read or change another user's data, and no background job writes anything for a deleted account.

## Non-goals

- Importing an export back into Alexandria, or any structured import format: bulk import is plain text (package 07), and an importer for other formats is a later PRD.
- Exporting settings, the AI key (or any part of it), personal access tokens, sessions or the import reports.
- Scheduled or automatic exports, or exports to a third-party service.
- Undoing an account deletion, a grace period, or soft deletion visible to the owner.
- Deleting individual parts of the library in bulk (other than the whole account).
- The data itself: accounts, links and uses (package 01), snapshots and reader views (02), summaries, tags, topics and the AI key (03), workspaces and notes (04), decay and liveness fields (05), the search index and topic and tag lists (06), imports (07).
- Sharing, collaboration or any cross-user feature.

## Background

After packages 01 to 07 the library stores, per user: the user record (email, display name) and its sessions and personal access tokens (01, `src/worker/auth/`); links, their use events and pin positions (01, `src/worker/links/`); fetch results, fetch history and the snapshots and reader views in the R2 bucket `SNAPSHOTS` under `u/{user_id}/` (02, `src/worker/fetcher/`); summaries, topics, tags and the encrypted AI provider key with its provider and model (03, `src/worker/enrich/`); workspaces, their membership and order, and workspace and link notes (04, `src/worker/workspaces/`); archive, dead and liveness fields and the decay thresholds (05, `src/worker/decay/`); the full-text search index (06, `src/worker/search/`); and imports with their reports (07, `src/worker/imports/`). Background work runs in the `FETCH_QUEUE` and `ENRICH_QUEUE` consumers, the import processing and the daily Cron Trigger. `GET /api/v1/links/{id}` returns a link with every field the packages add, and `GET /api/v1/links/{id}/reader` and `/snapshot` serve the reader view and snapshot while recording a use. There is no export and no way to delete an account; the settings page (`src/web/pages/Settings.tsx`) has the tokens, AI key, decay and import sections. Everything under `src/worker/account/` is new.

Constraints the owner has set:

- Constraint: no built-in user management; identity comes from Google sign-in, and deleting the account is the owner's own action.
- Constraint: strict per-user separation of data and processing.
- Constraint: TypeScript throughout, on Cloudflare Workers, D1, R2 and Queues.

## Requirements

### Export

- `GET` of the export returns a single JSON document with every link (all fields, all states, manual edits, use counts), workspace, topic and tag of the user; snapshots are not included in the JSON but each link carries a URL from which its snapshot and reader view can be fetched with the same token. For 20,000 links the export completes in under 60 seconds.
- The stored AI provider key is never included in the export.
- The settings page offers the export as a download.
- End-to-end flow: the owner downloads the export from the settings page; a script fetches one link's snapshot from the URL in the export with a personal access token.

### Account deletion

- From the settings page the user confirms deletion by typing their email address; every link, snapshot, workspace, token, session and the stored AI provider key of that user is removed, and the user record with them, within 10 minutes. The user is signed out immediately. There is no undo.
- Account deletion is the owner's alone: no other user, and no request that is not the owner's, can delete or read the account's data.
- End-to-end flow: the owner deletes the account from the settings page, is signed out at once, the owner's token stops working, and within 10 minutes nothing of the account remains.

## Design Decisions

1. **The export's snapshot and reader URLs record no use.** They point at `GET /api/v1/export/links/{id}/snapshot` and `GET /api/v1/export/links/{id}/reader`, which serve exactly what the reader and snapshot endpoints serve, with the same token, but record no use. Decided in this run: fetching 20,000 snapshots for a backup through the use-recording endpoints would reset the decay of the whole library.
2. **A link's export entry is its API representation.** Each entry is the body `GET /api/v1/links/{id}` returns, plus `snapshot_url` and `reader_url` (absolute on `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, `null` when there is nothing stored), so the export grows with every field a later package adds to the link. Decided in this run.
3. **The export is streamed and self-checking.** The document is written as it is read from D1, page by page, and its last member is `"complete": true`; a failure part-way aborts the stream, so a cut-off download never parses as a complete export. Decided in this run: 20,000 links do not fit a response built in memory within the time limit, and a truncated file must not pass for a full one.
4. **The export holds the user's email and name, links, workspaces, topics and tags and nothing else**: no settings, no AI key or any part of it, no tokens, sessions or import reports. Decided in this run: the source PRD lists what the export holds, and the key must never leave the server.
5. **Deleting the account needs a signed-in session.** `DELETE /api/v1/me` with a personal access token is refused with 403 `session_required`. Decided in this run: the source PRD puts deletion on the settings page, and a leaked token or an agent must not be able to destroy the library.
6. **Deletion is two-phase.** The request immediately deletes every session and token and the stored AI key, marks the account for deletion and queues the deletion job on a new queue, `ACCOUNT_QUEUE`; the job then removes the rest in batches, re-queueing itself until nothing remains, and removes the user record last. A Cron Trigger every 5 minutes re-runs the job for any account marked more than 5 minutes ago, so a lost or exhausted message cannot stop a deletion from finishing within 10 minutes. Decided in this run: a library of 20,000 links with snapshots is too much to delete within one request.
7. **The job finds the account's rows through the database itself.** It removes every row of the account from every table that holds a user or link reference, discovered from the schema rather than from a fixed list, so a table a later package adds is covered without changing the job. Decided in this run.
8. **Background work for an account marked for deletion does nothing.** Fetch, enrichment, import, liveness and decay work for such an account, or for a link that no longer exists, writes no row and no object and calls no external service. Decided in this run: otherwise a fetch finishing after the job could write a snapshot back.
9. **Signing in while a deletion is running is refused** with "Your account is being deleted, try again in a few minutes" (`/signin?error=deleting`); once the deletion has finished, the same Google account on the allow-list signs in to a new, empty library. Decided in this run.
10. **The confirmation compares the typed email case-insensitively, ignoring surrounding whitespace**; anything else is refused with 400 `confirmation_mismatch` and nothing is deleted. Decided in this run.

## Dependencies

- 01 `accounts_links_and_stream`: users, sessions, tokens, links, use events, the sign-in flow and page, the error envelope, the settings page.
- 02 `fetch_and_snapshot`: the snapshots and reader views in R2 and the fetch history; the fetch consumer that must write nothing for a deleted account.
- 03 `ai_enrichment`: summaries, topics, tags and the AI key; the enrichment consumer.
- 04 `workspaces_and_notes`: workspaces, membership and notes.
- 05 `decay_and_liveness`: the archive, dead and liveness fields and the decay settings; the daily cron's work.
- 06 `search_and_browse`: the search index, and the topic and tag lists the export reads.
- 07 `bulk_import`: imports and their processing.

External systems: Cloudflare D1, R2, Queues and Cron Triggers.

## Verified External API

No library beyond the project's own and the platform bindings: D1, R2 (`list` with a prefix, `delete` of up to 1,000 keys), Queues and Cron Triggers through `@cloudflare/workers-types`, and `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` 0.23.0 (`env`, `SELF`, `applyD1Migrations` from `cloudflare:test`) for the tests. The R2 and Queue binding methods are typed by `@cloudflare/workers-types` and were not read for this package.

## Glossary

- **export**: the single JSON document holding the owner's whole library, ending with `"complete": true`.
- **marked for deletion**: an account whose deletion was confirmed and whose data the deletion job is still removing.
- **deletion job**: the background work that removes a marked account's rows and objects in batches.
- **snapshot**: the raw HTML (or the whole PDF) stored at fetch time.
- **reader view**: the cleaned, content-only rendering extracted from the snapshot.
- **personal access token**: a user-created secret that authenticates API and MCP requests as that user.
- **AI key**: the user's own Anthropic or OpenRouter API key, stored for enrichment.

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN an authenticated user requests GET /api/v1/export, THE Alexandria API SHALL return one JSON document holding the user's email and display name, every link of the user, every workspace, every topic and every tag, ending with the member "complete": true, as a file download

   Check: unit

### REQ-2: Fetching stored content from the export

**Rationale:** A backup is only complete if the stored pages can be retrieved with it, and retrieving them must not count as using them.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN an authenticated user requests GET /api/v1/export/links/{id}/snapshot for one of their links, in any state including archived, that has a stored snapshot, THE Alexandria API SHALL serve the stored snapshot exactly as GET /api/v1/links/{id}/snapshot serves it, recording no use
   → HTTP 200 with the same status, Content-Type, Content-Security-Policy and body bytes as GET /api/v1/links/{id}/snapshot (text/html or application/pdf); the link's use_count and last_used_at are unchanged and no use event is added

1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN an authenticated user requests GET /api/v1/export/links/{id}/reader for one of their links, in any state including archived, that has a stored reader view, THE Alexandria API SHALL serve the stored reader view exactly as GET /api/v1/links/{id}/reader serves it, recording no use
   → HTTP 200 with the same Content-Type and body as GET /api/v1/links/{id}/reader; the link's use_count and last_used_at are unchanged and no use event is added

   → HTTP 202 with body {"status": "deleting"} and a Set-Cookie that expires 'alexandria_session'; the user's sessions and tokens rows are gone and the AI key column is empty; one message for the user is on ACCOUNT_QUEUE

1. [REQ-4.2] IF DELETE /api/v1/me carries no confirm_email or one that differs from the account's email, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL delete nothing and keep the user signed in

1. [REQ-4.3] IF DELETE /api/v1/me is authenticated by a personal access token rather than a session, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse the deletion and change nothing

### REQ-5: The deletion job

**Rationale:** Every trace of the account must go, however large the library and whatever fails on the way, and nothing of anyone else's.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN the deletion job runs for an account marked for deletion, THE account deletion worker SHALL remove every row that belongs to the account or to one of its links from every table of the database, found from the schema, and every R2 object under the account's prefix u/{user_id}/, and remove the user record last
   → afterwards no table has a row whose user id is the account's or whose link id is one of its former links, SNAPSHOTS lists no object under u/{user_id}/, and the users row is gone; every other user's rows and objects are unchanged
   Check: integration
   - setup: user A with links in every state, uses, fetch history, HTML and PDF snapshots and reader views, summaries, topics, tags, workspaces with notes, link notes, a finished import and an AI key; user B with the same kinds of data

   ```
   in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts: snapshotB = every row of every table (from sqlite_master) referencing B plus B's R2 listing with bodies; request A's deletion; run the ACCOUNT_QUEUE consumer until it stops re-queueing; for every table from sqlite_master with a user_id or link_id column assert no row references A or A's former link ids; assert SNAPSHOTS.list({prefix: 'u/' + A + '/'}) is empty and A's users row is gone; assert B's rows and objects equal snapshotB
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] THE account deletion worker SHALL remove a library of 20,000 links with a snapshot and a reader view each within 10 minutes of the deletion request, working in batches of at most 1,000 rows or objects and queueing the next batch until nothing remains
   Check: integration
   - setup: user A with 20,000 links, each with a stored snapshot and reader view in local R2
   ```
   in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts: t0 = performance.now(); request deletion; drive the ACCOUNT_QUEUE consumer message by message; assert no batch deletes more than 1,000 rows or objects; assert nothing of A remains and performance.now() - t0 < 600000
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] IF a run of the deletion job fails part-way, from a D1 or R2 error or the Worker's time limit, THEN THE account deletion worker SHALL leave what was already removed removed and let the retried run continue with what remains, restoring nothing
   → the consumer retries the message; the next run ends with nothing of the account remaining; a run on an account already fully deleted acknowledges its message and changes nothing

1. [REQ-5.4] WHEN the 5-minute Cron Trigger fires while an account has been marked for deletion for more than 5 minutes, THE scheduler SHALL run the deletion job for that account, so that a lost or exhausted queue message cannot stop the deletion from finishing
   → after the scheduled run and the batches it starts, nothing of the account remains; accounts marked less than 5 minutes ago are left to their queued job
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts: mark user A for deletion at now - 6 min and user C at now - 1 min with no queue messages; run the scheduled handler with cron '*/5 * * * *'; drive the queue; assert A is fully removed and C is untouched by the sweep
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: The owner exports the library and a script fetches a stored snapshot from it

1. **owner** chooses 'Export library' on the settings page
2. **website** downloads GET /api/v1/export as alexandria-export-<date>.json
3. **Alexandria API** streams the document with every link, workspace, topic and tag, ending with "complete": true
4. **script** reads the file and requests one link's snapshot_url with 'Authorization: Bearer <secret>'
5. **Alexandria API** serves the stored snapshot without recording a use
6. **owner** opens the link's detail page and sees its use count unchanged

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, D1 database, R2 snapshot store, the fetch worker, token authentication

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev with local D1, R2 and Queues; the owner signed in through e2e/fake-google.ts
- the owner has added two pages served by e2e/fake-origin.ts, fetched by the fetch worker, created a workspace holding one of them and a personal access token

**End state:**

- the downloaded file parses as JSON with two links, one workspace and complete: true
- the script's request to the first link's snapshot_url answered 200 with the HTML that e2e/fake-origin.ts served
- the link's use_count is the same before and after the script's request

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/export.spec.ts: sign in, add the two fake-origin pages, wait until they are no longer pending, create a workspace and a token; on /settings click 'Export library' and await the download; doc = JSON.parse(file); expect doc.links.length == 2 and doc.complete; before = doc.links[0].use_count; r = request.get(doc.links[0].snapshot_url, bearer); expect 200 and the fake page's HTML; expect request.get('/api/v1/links/' + id).use_count == before
```

### PATH-2: The owner deletes the account and nothing of it remains

1. **owner** types the account's email on the settings page and presses 'Delete account'
2. **website** sends DELETE /api/v1/me with the typed email
3. **Alexandria API** deletes every session, token and the AI key, marks the account for deletion, queues the deletion job and clears the session cookie
4. **website** shows the sign-in page saying the account and all its data are being deleted
5. **script** requests GET /api/v1/links with the owner's former token and is refused with 401
6. **account deletion worker** removes the account's rows and its R2 objects in batches and the user record last
7. **owner** signs in again with Google after the deletion has finished and finds an empty stream

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, account deletion worker, D1 database, R2 snapshot store, Queues, the fetch worker

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev with local D1, R2 and Queues; ALLOWED_EMAILS includes owner@example.test; the owner signed in through e2e/fake-google.ts
- the owner has two fetched links with snapshots served by e2e/fake-origin.ts, a workspace, a personal access token and an AI key accepted by e2e/fake-ai.ts

**End state:**

- the browser was at /signin?deleted=1 immediately after the button was pressed
- the script's request with the former token got 401 {"error": "unauthorized"}
- within 10 minutes no D1 row references the former user or its links, and the local R2 bucket holds no object under its prefix
- the second sign-in created a new user whose stream is empty

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/account-deletion.spec.ts: set up the library; type the email on /settings and press 'Delete account'; expect url '/signin?deleted=1'; expect request.get('/api/v1/links', bearer).status == 401; poll `wrangler d1 execute --local` for rows referencing the old user id and the local R2 listing for the prefix until both are empty, failing after 10 minutes; sign in again; expect zero cards
```

## Dependencies

- `01` — exports and deletes its users, sessions, tokens, links and use events, extends its sign-in flow and settings page, and uses its error envelope
- `02` — serves and deletes its snapshots and reader views in R2, and stops its fetch consumer writing for a deleted account
- `03` — exports its summaries, topics and tags, deletes the AI key, and stops its enrichment consumer for a deleted account
- `04` — exports and deletes its workspaces, membership and notes
- `05` — exports its archive and liveness fields and stops its daily decay and liveness work for a deleted account
- `06` — deletes its search index rows and exports the topic and tag lists it maintains
- `07` — deletes its imports and stops import processing for a deleted account

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-3

- 1.2 Implement GET /api/v1/export in src/worker/account/export.ts as a streamed response: the header members, then the links read page by page in id order, then workspaces with their link ids in manual order, topics and tags with their link counts, and the closing member "complete": true, with Content-Disposition naming alexandria-export-<date>.json
- 1.3 Build each link entry from the same serialiser GET /api/v1/links/{id} uses, so that every field a package adds to the link is exported, and add snapshot_url and reader_url on PUBLIC_ORIGIN, or null when nothing is stored
- 1.4 Leave out the AI key in every form, token secrets and hashes, session identifiers, import reports and settings, and read only the requesting user's rows
- 1.5 On a read failure part-way, error the stream so the download fails and never ends with "complete": true
